source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 15, 16a, 20a, 27, 28a, 28b, 29: Instr PDF p.22 line 28a qualification ('Your income on line 27 is $150,000 or less'), PDF p.23 Worksheet D first question (line 27 MORE than $150,000); GIT-1 & 2 p.21 example ($150,450); PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 160,000.00 (wages 55,000.00 + pensions 60,000.00 + 40,000.00 + interest 5,000.00); federal taxable income = 160,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 128,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 15 wages 55,000.00 + line 16a interest 5,000.00 + line 20a pensions 100,000.00 = line 27 total income 160,000.00; measure 160,000.00, over 150,000, keep share 0. Line 28a: line 27 is more than 150,000, so no pension exclusion: 0.00. Line 28b: Worksheet D answers Yes to 'line 27 MORE than $150,000', so no unclaimed exclusion (and wages are over 3,000): 0.00. Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 160,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 160,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 2 (nobody is 65 or older, so no senior exemption) = 2,000.00; line 38 = 2,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 160,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 158,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table B (joint/head of household/qualifying widow(er)) as bands: 20,000.00 x 0.014 = 280.00 + 30,000.00 x 0.0175 = 525.00 + 20,000.00 x 0.0245 = 490.00 + 10,000.00 x 0.035 = 350.00 + 70,000.00 x 0.05525 = 3,867.50 + 8,000.00 x 0.0637 = 509.60 = 6,022.10. No credits. State income tax = 6,022.10. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty.
